name: FM depth and LFO mix evolving chase sequence
goal: Keep long cinematic chase/arp-like sequences alive by modulating FM depth, oscillator mix via LFOs, and filter cutoff — plus mod-wheel/aftertouch for tension — instead of static one-bar loops.

source.title: TRAVELER Track Walkthrough by Venus Theory

prerequisites: Hybrid synth or Traveler-inspired Web Audio engine with multi-osc, stereo filter, envelopes, LFOs/mod matrix, sequenced control tracks (or automation), and FX (EQ/chorus/delay/reverb)

inputs.name: fm_pair
inputs.description: Carrier/modulator pair for FM depth play

constraints: Original synthesis only; not affiliated with KeySolutions; do not rip Traveler samples/presets/wavetables.
Original synthesis only — design new patches from portable parameters; do not copy proprietary Traveler factory preset names, banks, wavetables, or samples.
Not affiliated with KeySolutions Sounds or Traveler; concepts mapped to generic hybrid-synth / Web Audio equivalents.
Do not rip, dump, or redistribute Traveler content.
Prefer recreating the described signal-flow and motion relationships in our browser music system or any hybrid synth with comparable modules.

steps.action: Establish rhythmic pulse/sequence foundation (arp or control-track → cutoff). Aim for cinematic intensity rather than clean EDM purity.
Introduce FM: vary modulator frequency slightly and automate/modulate FM depth so timbre breathes over the phrase.
Use LFOs to change oscillator mix balances over time; also modulate filter cutoff so the sequence refuses to feel static across long cues.
steps.expect: Ongoing evolution without constant DAW drawing

steps.action: Assign mod wheel / aftertouch to open tension (depth, cutoff, or drive) for scene dynamics.
Play deeper registers for more body when the cue needs weight; keep FX (delay bounce) feeding syncopated rhythms for living grooves.
steps.expect: Register and delay accent the chase

verification: Disabling FM/LFO mix returns a flatter loop
Useful across long film/game cue lengths
